correctness.rationale: The differentiated binomial kernel yields an exact polynomial numerator. The two real torus equations and explicit factorization identify boundary crossings. Every strict subcritical torus root is nondegenerate and persists inside by the real implicit-function theorem. Above threshold, a uniform zero-free large-coefficient limit and a connected zero-count argument on each variable exclude any bidisk root. Rouché continuity treats equality. Pure value and pure derivative cases and beta=1 are verified analytically, with algebra corroborated by the reproducible checker.

value.rationale: The natural first-order Gram nonvanishing question on the canonical fractional binomial complete Pick family has an exact global sharp answer. The unexpected nonmonotone transition—pure jet zero-free, intermediate mixture having zeros, sufficiently large derivative mixture zero-free—defines a structural phenomenon distinct from beta=2 and explains its disappearance at the Hardy endpoint. The classification covers a continuum of exponents and all complex coefficient pairs.
